description: Direct Speech presents the speaker's exact words as they are. Indirect Speech conveys the same message in our own words without changing its meaning.

sections.title: Basic Concepts and Structure
sections.description: It is essential to understand the main parts of Direct Speech to change them correctly.

key_concepts.explanation: The part of the sentence outside the quotation marks that tells who is speaking to whom. Example: 'He said'.
The actual words spoken by the speaker, enclosed within quotation marks.

grammar_rules.explanation: When changing to Indirect Speech, the comma and inverted commas are removed, and a conjunction like 'that' is used in assertive sentences.

sections.title: Rules for Change of Tense
sections.description: If the Reporting Verb is in the Past Tense, the tense of the Reported Speech also changes to the Past Tense.

grammar_rules.structure: Simple Present -> Simple Past, Present Continuous -> Past Continuous
grammar_rules.explanation: All present tenses in the Reported Speech change to their corresponding past tenses.

grammar_rules.structure: Simple Past -> Past Perfect, Past Continuous -> Past Perfect Continuous
grammar_rules.explanation: Simple Past is changed to Past Perfect, and Past Continuous to Past Perfect Continuous.

examples.correct_or_usage: He said that he wrote a letter.
examples.explanation: Since the Reporting Verb 'said' is in the past tense, 'write' (Simple Present) is changed to 'wrote' (Simple Past).

examples.incorrect_or_context: She said, 'I was reading a book.'
examples.correct_or_usage: She said that she had been reading a book.
examples.explanation: Past Continuous (was reading) is changed to Past Perfect Continuous (had been reading).

sections.title: Changes in Pronouns and Time/Place Words
sections.description: Words indicating person, time, or place are changed according to the context.

key_concepts.explanation: 'Now' changes to 'then', 'here' to 'there', 'today' to 'that day', and 'tomorrow' to 'the next day'.

grammar_rules.structure: 1st Person -> Subject, 2nd Person -> Object, 3rd Person -> No Change
grammar_rules.explanation: First Person pronouns in Reported Speech change according to the Subject of the Reporting Verb, Second Person according to the Object, and Third Person pronouns remain unchanged.

examples.incorrect_or_context: He said to me, 'You are my best friend.'
examples.correct_or_usage: He told me that I was his best friend.
examples.explanation: 'You' (2nd Person) changes to 'I' according to the object 'me', and 'my' (1st Person) changes to 'his' according to the subject 'He'.

sections.title: Interrogative Sentences
sections.description: Special rules are followed when converting interrogative sentences into Indirect Speech.

grammar_rules.structure: Yes/No Questions -> if/whether, Wh- Questions -> Wh- word
grammar_rules.explanation: Use 'if' or 'whether' for questions starting with a helping verb. For questions starting with 'Wh-' words, do not use any other conjunction; the 'Wh-' word itself acts as the conjunction.

examples.incorrect_or_context: She said to him, 'Are you going?'
examples.correct_or_usage: She asked him if he was going.
examples.explanation: The interrogative sentence is changed to an assertive sentence, and 'if' is used instead of 'that'.

strategies.title: Change Sentence Type
strategies.detail: Change the interrogative structure (Verb + Subject) into an assertive structure (Subject + Verb), remove the question mark, and add a full stop.

sections.title: Imperative and Exclamatory Sentences
sections.description: Conversion of sentences expressing commands, requests, advice, and strong emotions.

grammar_rules.explanation: Change 'said to' according to the mood of the sentence and place the infinitive 'to' before the main verb.

grammar_rules.structure: Reporting Verb (exclaimed with joy/sorrow) + that + Assertive Sentence
grammar_rules.explanation: Change the Reporting Verb according to the emotion, use 'that', and remove exclamatory words like Alas, Hurrah, or Wow.

examples.incorrect_or_context: The captain said to the soldiers, 'Stand at ease.'
examples.correct_or_usage: The captain commanded the soldiers to stand at ease.
examples.explanation: This is a command, so 'commanded' is used, and 'to' acts as the conjunction.

sections.title: Exceptions
sections.description: In certain specific situations, the general rule of changing the tense does not apply.

exceptions.explanation: If the Reported Speech states a universal truth, scientific fact, or idiom, its tense does not change, even if the reporting verb is in the past tense.
exceptions.example: Direct: The teacher said, 'The sun rises in the east.' -> Indirect: The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.

exceptions.explanation: If the Reporting Verb is in the Present or Future tense, the tense of the Reported Speech remains unchanged.
exceptions.example: Direct: She says, 'I am ready.' -> Indirect: She says that she is ready.
